mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% over the prior 10 trading days reduces discount rates applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rate hike events, or the 10-day moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 2.25% during the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the labor signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX returns is <0.3 in a regression with controls for inflation and GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing demand, which lowers growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO declines by >2% in three months, or the signal reverts before the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 293 for two consecutive months suggests the Federal Reserve may pivot to rate cuts, lowering borrowing costs and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 293 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL falling below 293 for two months, or the SPX move is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it indicates a tightening cycle that increases the real discount rate, reducing the present value of future equities and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar events, or the 3-month FEDFUNDS average never exceeds 4% during the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in weekly job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies but implied by a combination of PAYEMS and UNRATE dynamics) coupled with a sharp drop in the unemployment rate suggests a labor market transition toward expansion, which elevates equity risk premia and drives positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.3pp while PAYEMS increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the labor signal, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to 'late-cycle expansion' characterized by rising consumer confidence (implied by CPIAUCSL and HOUST) and sustained industrial production (INDPRO) above 105, produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days regardless of interest rate path.
candidate_trigger: regime: late-cycle expansion (defined by CPIAUCSL > 295, HOUST > 1400, INDPRO > 105 for 3 months)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in the late-cycle expansion regime, or the regime is not confirmed by the defined proxy thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: During a 'monetary easing fatigue' regime where FEDFUNDS remains above 3% for 4 consecutive months, the equity risk aversion parameter does not decline, so S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days are expected to be negative as investors anticipate no further rate cuts.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when FEDFUNDS stays above 3% for 4 months, or the SPX move is explained by factors other than risk aversion (e.g., sector rotation).
